symptom: After `mxcli layout`, entity boxes overlapped in Studio Pro: a tall box stacked above a short one ran into it, and `mxcli layout --only-overlapping` reported nothing to move for real collisions (a 22-attribute entity at (100,380) running into one at (100,660); a 45-attribute entity at (880,100) into one at (880,660)).
cause: dmlayout assumed an entity's Location is the CENTRE of its box (the package comment cited RelativeMiddlePoint). That field belongs to microflow objects; a domain-model entity stores Location and Studio Pro 11.12.5 draws it as the box's TOP-LEFT corner (entities created at the same Y with 4, 30 and 45 attributes share one top edge). Plan added half a box to every position and the overlap check centred each box, so both were half a box off in x and y.
fix: Plan places each entity at the corner of its slot (no half-box); entityRect and nearestFree treat Location as the top-left corner, and a mover is rejected only for negative coordinates. Annotation obstacles keep their both-conventions cover because that convention is unverified.
insight: **A coordinate convention is a fact about the file format, so verify it against the application, not against a similarly named field**: `RelativeMiddlePoint` (centre) is the microflow-object field, an entity's `Location` is its top-left. Cheap check: create entities at the same Location.Y with different attribute counts and look at whether the top edges or the centres line up; a test that only agrees with the code's own convention proves nothing, so the regression test sizes boxes independently with the measured geometry (150 wide, 34 + 15 per attribute).
